text:
Priya Nair: Quick follow-up from the offload async RFC — I sketched a lightweight 'slab gardener' that sits between the KV prefix cache and the allocator. Goal: reclaim cold KV entries across tenants without triggering full-page migrations or noisy global GC.

Alex Chen: curious, how is gardener different from the current evictor? sounds like a hybrid compactor? :thinking:

Priya Nair: Good Q. It's policy-first not scanner-first. Instead of scanning all resident pages, gardener maintains small hotness fingerprints per slab and a compact per-tenant bloom-like map. When a slab's hotness drops below threshold, gardener schedules incremental local compaction (within slab) and selectively demotes KV entries to host-backed pages. No global stop-the-world.

Michael Park: can you paste the pseudo-config? want to understand safety margins for latency-sensitive tenants.

Priya Nair: Sure — current prototype knobs:
```
gardener.enabled = true
gardener.hot_window_secs = 30
gardener.compact_batch_size = 64   # number of KV slots to consider per tick
gardener.demote_latency_budget_ms = 10
gardener.soft_pin_ttl_ms = 5000
```
Policy: per-tenant soft-pin prevents demotion of newly touched items for soft_pin_ttl. compact_batch_size bound keeps background work CPU-friendly.

Jen Ortega: demote_latency_budget_ms sounds tight — are we measuring token-latency tail impact? if demotion touches hot cache path we could regress p99.

Priya Nair: Agreed. Planner enforces two invariants: (1) never demote if recent access rate > hot_threshold, (2) pace demotion when GPU QPS spike detected. We expose a circuit-breaker that pauses gardener when tail latency > SLO.

Alex Chen: what about fragmentation? compacting KV within slab can increase free contiguous pages but we still need page-level migration for large tensors. Does gardener coordinate with the offload subsystem to avoid double work?

Priya Nair: Yes — gardener emits minimal intents (``DEMOTE_CANDIDATE slab_id:slot_list``). Offload controller subscribes and schedules actual page-level migration if a contiguous eviction window forms. If offload already has an incoming migration, gardener suppresses overlaps.

Michael Park: sounds racey. how do we prevent race where gardener demotes a slot while a live inference references it?

Priya Nair: We use lease tokens on KV slots. Live inference increments slot lease; gardener only finalizes demotion when lease==0. Lease ops are cheap atomic increments in the runtime path. There is also a fallback: if finalization times out, gardener reverts to a mark-and-sweep with safe pin.

Alex Chen: sketch the lease lifecycle please — is it per-request or per-kv-handle?

Priya Nair: Per-kv-handle + per-request bump for short critical sections. Typical flow: request pins handle (inc), runtime uses KV -> releases (dec). For longer pinned contexts (e.g., streaming generation), we attach a soft_pin which gardener respects and extends.

Jen Ortega: telemetry plan? we need to track gardener-induced demotes, rollbacks, and correlation with p99 spikes.

Priya Nair: Plan: add three counters and a histogram: gardener.demote_attempts, gardener.demote_success, gardener.demote_revert_reason (labelled), and demote_latency_ms histogram. Also emit correlation events: {slot_age, tenant_id, qps_bucket, demote_outcome}.

Michael Park: performance question — bloom-like map per slab is extra RAM. budget?

Priya Nair: We sized it as 64B per slab by default. For a 4k slabs pool that's ~256KB — negligible. We can make it adaptive per-tenant.

Alex Chen: can we get a short PoC with a toggle and a canary tenant next week? I'll pair on telemetry.

Priya Nair: yes, I'll push a WIP branch. gardener-bot: scheduled canary for tenant "alpha" on staging at 2023-04-07 03:00 UTC.

gardener-bot: :white_check_mark: canary created (id=gardener-canary-142). will report demote metrics to /dash/gardener/canary.

Jen Ortega: cool — add a kill-switch env var so SRE can hot-disable.

Priya Nair: will do. thanks all for quick feedback. I'll share design doc and a minimal API for lease ops tomorrow. :thumbsup:
